This means that unless someone actually benchmarks this we cannot say for sure whether it is 6%, less, more, linear, or not. <vbuterin> Well we can tell from simple theoretical reasoning that tree construction is linear and is ~1 two-chunk-sized hash per chunk That is roughly what we have there 🙂 Personally I am in favour of having "nice" equations, but I can understand the position to have some fixed cost per chunk instead. <vbuterin> The thing is that there's like 12 EIPs coming out, so it's important for each of them to try to be "just parameter changes" as much as possible 😃 <vbuterin> And code merklization by default is actually really simple; it just replaces code hashing with another pure function (that you can probably write a 20-line python impl of) <vbuterin> Even the gas cost of hashing itself is not a "nice equation"; given how merkle-damgard and sponge work it "should" be chunk-based but we just charge per byte 😂 > <vbuterin> This seems to not specify how nextChunk.startOffset is set That is mentioned in the intro section: > Note that startOffset corresponds to the absolute program counter, and firstInstructionOffset is the offset within the chunk to the first instruction, as opposed to data. <vbuterin> right I see <vbuterin> adding the 20-line python impl into the EIP would probably make it super-clean 😆 The truth is, it was a typescript snippet, translated into text, and the snipped moved into the implementation section. We knew Python is what many people prefer, but we're not really good with Python. If anyone wants to draft up a short python-esque pseudo code, please do! <@!425343240212971521> did write a complete Python version linked in the implementation section: https://github.com/hugo-dc/code-chunks/blob/master/main.py > <vbuterin> Even the gas cost of hashing itself is not a "nice equation"; given how merkle-damgard and sponge work it "should" be chunk-based but we just charge per byte 😂 Actually we charge per word (32-bytes), while keccak-256 sponge is larger than that Thanks for the feedback! It is late here, will respond to anything else in the morning <vbuterin> def generate_code_root(program): return treefy(chunkify(program), len(program)) def chunkify(program): chunks = [] pos = 0 this_chunk_start = 0 this_chunk_code_start = 0 while pos < len(program): pos += (program[pos] - 0x5f) if (0x60 <= program[pos] <= 0x7f) else 1 if pos >= this_chunk_start + 32: chunks.append(hash(program[this_chunk_start: this_chunk_start+32] + this_chunk_code_start.to_bytes(32, 'big'))) this_chunk_start += 32 this_chunk_code_start = pos return chunks def next_power_of_2(x): return x if x <= 2 else next_power_of_2((x +1) // 2) * 2 def treefy(chunks, length): padded_length = next_power_of_2(len(chunks)) tree = [None] * padded_length + chunks + [b'\x00'*32] * (padded_length - len(chunks)) for i in range(padded_length-1, 0, -1): tree[i] = hash(tree[i*2] + tree[i*2+1]) metadata = length.to_bytes(32, 'big') return hash(tree[1] + metadata) <vbuterin> There's a draft, I coded it in this chat so zero testing and I'm sure there's a bug and it doesn't follow the spec faithfully 👀 That's awesome! Will chew on this in the morning 🙂 This code uses a nice trick for complete binary trees. If you store the nodes as an array in breadth-first order, then the node at index `i` has children at indices `2i` and `2i+1`. (Irrelevant for this discussion, but more fun facts: the node at index `i` has parent at index `floor(i/2)` , and these formulas are a special case of more general formulas for complete k-ary trees, where integer k>2.) Complete binary trees have a maximum number of nodes at every depth, except maybe the bottommost depth where only the rightmost nodes are absent. Like this. ``` x / \ / \ x x / \ / \ x x x x / \ | x x x ```

excerpts.content:
<vbuterin> def generate_code_root(program):
    return treefy(chunkify(program), len(program))
def chunkify(program):
    chunks = []
    pos = 0
    this_chunk_start = 0
    this_chunk_code_start = 0
    while pos < len(program):
        pos += (program[pos] - 0x5f) if (0x60 <= program[pos] <= 0x7f) else 1
        if pos >= this_chunk_start + 32:
            chunks.append(hash(program[this_chunk_start: this_chunk_start+32] + this_chunk_code_start.to_bytes(32, 'big')))
            this_chunk_start += 32
            this_chunk_code_start = pos
    return chunks
def next_power_of_2(x):
    return x if x <= 2 else next_power_of_2((x +1) // 2) * 2
def treefy(chunks, length):
    padded_length = next_power_of_2(len(chunks))
    tree = [None] * padded_length + chunks + [b'\x00'*32] * (padded_length - len(chunks))
    for i in range(padded_length-1, 0, -1):
        tree[i] = hash(tree[i*2] + tree[i*2+1])
    metadata = length.to_bytes(32, 'big')
    return hash(tree[1] + metadata)
